nodes.label: Action Side-Effect Graph Rule
nodes.summary: Every order/payment/customer action must propagate to every dependent system (inventory, coupon, affiliate, loyalty, notifications, customer timeline) — treat mutations as graph traversals, not point updates.

nodes.label: Inventory Restore on Reversal
nodes.summary: On any order reversal, restore Product.inventory + ProductVariant.inventory using raw-SQL FOR UPDATE inside $transaction with an inventoryHistory row typed 'return_stock' to avoid lost-update races.

nodes.label: Coupon Usage Decrement on Reversal
nodes.summary: Decrement Coupon.usageCount with a gt:0 floor guard on reversal — prevents concurrent refunds driving the count negative.

nodes.label: Affiliate Commission Reversal
nodes.summary: Call affiliateService.reverseCommission(storeId, orderId) as a no-op-safe primitive — idempotent if commission was never paid or already reversed.

nodes.label: Loyalty Points Reversal
nodes.summary: LoyaltyService.reverseEarnedPointsFromOrder is idempotent via a tagged 'refund-revoke:<earnId>' adjust transaction — double-revoke is blocked by tag lookup.

nodes.label: Customer Profile Timeline
nodes.summary: Any action touching a customer's money must appear on the customer detail page — stats, chips, and inline rows — driven by widening the API include, not the page render.

nodes.label: Inngest Fan-out for Notifications
nodes.summary: All post-action notification channels (email, WhatsApp/SMS dispatcher, OneSignal push) fire via a single Inngest event with Promise.allSettled steps — never bespoke-wire channels at the callsite.

nodes.label: Refund Side-Effect Pipeline
nodes.summary: All three Ebda Store refund paths (admin Refund via provider, gateway webhook, manual status) converge on OrderService.applyRefundEffects() which runs all six reversals and fires the order/refunded Inngest event.

nodes.label: Admin Refund via Provider Button
nodes.summary: POST /stores/:id/orders/:orderId/refund-via-provider calls PaymentService.refund which moves real money at the provider before converging on applyRefundEffects — only visible when paymentStatus=paid and a completed online payment row exists.

nodes.label: Gateway Webhook Refund Path
nodes.summary: Provider-initiated refund webhooks route through PaymentService.handleWebhook then converge on applyRefundEffects — same six side-effects for free without additional callsite code.

nodes.label: Manual Refunded Status Path
nodes.summary: Admin setting order status to 'refunded' via OrderService.updateStatus also calls applyRefundEffects — before 2026-05-16 this path only flipped DB rows without reversing inventory, coupon, or loyalty.

nodes.label: order/refunded Inngest Function
nodes.summary: order-refunded-fanout sends customer refund email (branded shell, bilingual), dispatches notification channels via refund_processed template, and fires OneSignal admin push with data.type='order.refunded'.

nodes.label: Refund Reason Propagation
nodes.summary: Admin types reason in RefundButton modal → persisted to Payment.metadata.refundReason → Inngest function reads it once and distributes to customer email, dispatcher template, and admin push body.

nodes.label: Webhook URL Drift Bug-Class
nodes.summary: Internal callsites built webhookUrl without /api/v1 prefix and /:provider suffix, diverging from what the admin UI showed merchants — silent broken webhooks for providers that honor the field.

nodes.label: Single Webhook URL Builder Rule
nodes.summary: When an admin UI displays a URL the user copies into an external system, the same value must come from the same builder server-side — extract paymentWebhookUrl(provider) to a shared helper to prevent drift.

nodes.label: Cart Shipping Form Field Order (Egypt)
nodes.summary: Storefront checkout uses firstName/lastName/phone/email(optional)/area/address1/address2 with no city field — Egypt deliveries route on area only, city field removed to reduce mobile checkout friction.

nodes.label: Optional Email in Checkout
nodes.summary: Email is optional in the storefront checkout (phone-link customers don't always have email) — API addressSchema relaxed to z.string().email().optional().or(z.literal('')), format-validated only when filled.

nodes.label: Admin vs Storefront Form Divergence
nodes.summary: Admin phone-order form keeps the City field (staff have time to fill it); storefront drops it — intentional split where the admin tool targets merchants with time, and storefront targets customers mid-tap.

nodes.label: Wady Aljuz MyFatoorah Live
nodes.summary: Wady Aljuz can accept MyFatoorah payments end-to-end after saving the per-store webhook secret via admin Payment Settings — stored AES-encrypted in PaymentConfig.webhookSecret, decrypted at runtime.

nodes.label: Per-Store Webhook Secret Pattern
nodes.summary: Payment provider webhook secrets are stored per-store via admin UI (not Railway env vars) — AES-encrypted in PaymentConfig.webhookSecret, loaded by factory.getProvider() at webhook-verify time.

nodes.label: MyFatoorah Webhook Chain
nodes.summary: Full verified chain: customer pays → MyFatoorah POSTs → resolveStoreIdFromWebhookPayload → per-store PaymentConfig loaded → HMAC-SHA256 verified → Payment/Order updated → Inngest order/created fires fan-out.

nodes.label: HMAC Failure P0 Alert
nodes.summary: 3 HMAC failures in 5 minutes from the same provider+store triggers a P0 Telegram alert — catches portal-side webhook secret rotation before merchants notice missed payments.

nodes.label: Refresh Payment Safety Net
nodes.summary: Admin Refresh Payment button re-asks the provider for payment status and runs the same Inngest fanout the webhook would have — escape hatch when webhooks miss due to misconfiguration, rotation, or network blip.

nodes.label: Inngest Event Re-fire on Manual Refresh
nodes.summary: Refresh Payment re-fires order/created so customer/admin get email+push even when the webhook never arrived — Inngest's per-store concurrency key prevents double-send if a delayed webhook later arrives.

nodes.label: Public API Variant Include Gap
nodes.summary: listPublic and advancedSearch omitted variants from their Prisma include, causing every product to silently render as single-SKU even after variant features shipped — TypeScript cannot catch this class of missing-include bug.

nodes.label: Silent Feature Degradation via Missing Prisma Include
nodes.summary: Any UI feature that branches on obj.relation?.length will silently fall to the no-relation branch if any endpoint forgets to include the relation — audit Prisma include trees for every endpoint the UI consumes when shipping relation-dependent features.

nodes.label: Narrow Variant Select on Public Endpoints
nodes.summary: Public product endpoints include variants with select:{id, price, compareAtPrice} only — provides the 3 fields getProductPricing needs while keeping payload small for storefront performance.
